domain_label: Turlock Independent Health & Wellness — Business Models & Unit Economics
purpose: A method for reasoning about how each independent health-and-wellness format in Turlock and Stanislaus County is actually run as a business — its clinical or studio offering and capital equipment, its W-2-versus-owner-operator-versus-1099 labor model, its healing-arts-board and Denti-Cal/AB-5 licensing gate, its supplier and buying-group chain, and its labeled benchmark revenue and margin — split across the two economic engines (insurance-reimbursed clinical versus cash/membership wellness), without ever stating a named business's dollar revenue, payer mix or owner income as fact.
assumptions: no observed per-business financials supplied; every dollar band is a labeled industry-benchmark estimate (revenue per provider/practice/studio, overhead %, COGS %) scaled by an observable size signal (provider count, format) and a Central-Valley reimbursement/cost-of-living haircut, tagged estimate-not-actual, never a claim of actual revenue for any named business

the universe is the 26 verified independent health-and-wellness businesses in Turlock catalogued in businesses.json (chains, DSOs, hospital-employed providers and corporate optical excluded) across six sub-categories, in a town of ~72,500 with ~9,700 CSU Stanislaus students and a large county ag/warehouse and retiree musculoskeletal-demand base

city, county, state and demographic figures used here (population, income, ancestry shares, license/renewal fees, the 2026 Medicare PT conversion factor) are cited public facts from the deep-dive or labeled derivations, not invented

supplier-to-named-business links are representative inference about the realistic supply universe (the dental big three, EssilorLuxottica/ABB, ScripHessco/MeyerDC), not confirmed contracts, unless a cited source states the relationship

cost-structure and margin benchmarks are published industry figures (ADA HPI, optometry GPO/COGS surveys, APTA/WebPT, boutique-fitness and yoga operating models) applied as planning priors, not audited operator P&Ls
exclusions: chains, DSOs, hospital-employed providers and corporate/online optical (the catalog is independents only)
stating any actual dollar revenue, collections, payer mix or owner income for a specifically named Turlock business as fact
demand-and-saturation market sizing as a standalone deliverable beyond what is needed to judge a format's viability (the per-10k saturation detail lives in the market/reconciled analyses)
non-clinical retail health products, pharmacy, and med-spa/aesthetic injectables except where a wellness format straddles into a cash-service arm
tax, legal, immigration and clinical-licensing advice for an individual provider; this models formats and decisions, not a specific filing or treatment

glossary.definition: The binding honesty label on every dollar band in this KB: the figure is a published industry benchmark (revenue per provider/practice/studio, overhead %, COGS %) scaled by an observable Turlock size signal and a Central-Valley reimbursement/cost-of-living haircut, never a reported or claimed actual revenue, collections or owner income for any named business.

The structural split of this sector into insurance-reimbursed clinical (dental, optometry, PT, the PI slice of chiropractic) gated by payer contracts, and cash/membership wellness (gyms, yoga, barre, the cash/maintenance slice of chiropractic) gated by utilization; the two have different supply chains, labor models and binding constraints.

The share of optometry patients who buy frames/lenses/contacts in-practice rather than at Costco or online; the optical-margin engine of an independent OD practice, because the exam itself is near-break-even and 27-35% optical COGS is recovered only on captured eyewear.

A Medi-Cal dental provider enrollment that is separate from and additional to DDS licensure, required before a Turlock dental practice can bill the low-income majority; Denti-Cal reimburses well below commercial PPO and carries heavier admin, so the enrollment-and-mix decision sets the dental margin.

The California Dynamex/ABC-test worker-classification rule that exposes the 1099-per-class-paid instructor model used by gyms, barre and yoga studios to reclassification and back-pay risk; the binding non-fee gate every studio entrant must resolve before scaling.

The ~$33.40 per-RVU Medicare physician/therapy conversion factor for 2026 (net roughly -1% after RVU changes), the per-visit reimbursement headwind that compresses physical-therapy margin and means PT growth must come from referral volume, not rate.

The demand cap created by Modesto (~15 minutes north, Memorial/Doctors hospital systems, specialist and chain optical, multi-provider dental groups) siphoning higher-acuity and price-shopping clinical demand out of Turlock, the single biggest force keeping the catalog ratio below the provider benchmark.

The demand floor created by Assyrian (~20k), Portuguese/Azorean (~7.3%) and Punjabi/Hispanic (46%) trust-and-language pools plus multigenerational family-practice loyalty (Mas Vida bilingual, Generations/Plett family practices) that fragments demand into parallel pools each supporting its own independent above the raw per-capita benchmark.

An observable proxy (inferable provider count, format, single-versus-multi-provider, scope of advertised procedures) used to scale a published per-provider or per-practice benchmark into a planning revenue band, in place of unavailable actual collections.

glossary.term: high gross is not high net
glossary.definition: The pairing rule that every high revenue band (a multi-provider or oral-surgery dental office grossing toward $1M+) is reported with its thin-net/overhead caveat (dental overhead 55-80% of collections, PT and clinic single-digit net) so a high revenue band is never read as high profit.

nodes.definition: Establish the demand floor every Turlock health-and-wellness format draws on: ~72,500 residents at a median household income of ~$82,995 and median age ~34.9, ~9,700 CSU Stanislaus students whose younger, vision-and-wellness-skewed cohort lifts optometry and fitness/yoga demand, and a large county ag, warehouse and retiree base that drives musculoskeletal (chiropractic, physical therapy) volume above a white-collar town's baseline. Demand splits structurally into the insurance-reimbursed clinical engine (dental, optometry, PT) and the semi-discretionary cash/membership wellness engine (gyms, yoga, the cash slice of chiropractic), the first recession-resilient and the second the first line cut in a downturn. This is the size and shape of demand before any format question is asked.

included: resident population, income, median age
CSU Stanislaus student demand
ag/warehouse/retiree musculoskeletal demand
the clinical-versus-cash demand split

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a population, income, enrollment, or ag-workforce figure is updated

pros.claim: Sizing demand from cited public figures and the two-engine split grounds every format judgment in real local demand instead of national job-board noise
pros.example: the ag/warehouse/retiree base explains why chiropractic and PT volume runs above a white-collar town's baseline

cons.claim: A demand floor invites the error of treating semi-discretionary cash demand as recession-resilient like clinical demand
cons.example: reading yoga/fitness membership demand as stable when it is the first wallet cut in a downturn

failure_modes: treating the resident base as the independents' addressable revenue without subtracting Modesto leakage and chain capture
ignoring the clinical-versus-cash engine split and modeling both on one resilience assumption
acceptance_tests: the demand base cites population, income, median age, student enrollment and the ag/retiree musculoskeletal driver, and names the clinical-versus-cash two-engine split, labeled estimate where derived
revisit_triggers: a Census ACS refresh changes population or income
CSU Stanislaus enrollment shifts materially
the local ag/warehouse employment base shifts

nodes.definition: Tie Turlock's heritage depth and family-practice loyalty to the formats it sustains above the raw per-capita benchmark. The town holds California's largest Assyrian community (~20,000, ~25% of the city), a ~7.3% Portuguese/Azorean cohort, and Punjabi/Sikh and Mexican (~46% Hispanic) communities, each forming a trust-and-language pool that fragments demand into parallel sub-markets. The clearest visible evidence is Mas Vida Chiropractic's explicit bilingual (English/Spanish) positioning and the multigenerational family-named practices (Generations Family Optometry, Plett Family Optometry, the family-dentistry cluster, Turlock Eyecare since 1950). This community-expander floor is what keeps the count from collapsing toward chain dominance and lets a 73k town carry more independents per capita than the benchmark predicts.

included: Assyrian, Portuguese/Azorean, Punjabi/Hispanic ancestry shares with sources
family-dynasty multigenerational loyalty
the bilingual and family-named practice evidence
the per-capita over-indexing it explains
excluded: the cost structure of each format

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a community's size or a family-practice succession changes

pros.claim: Mapping trust-and-language pools and family loyalty to practices explains why the count exceeds the raw per-capita benchmark
pros.example: Mas Vida's bilingual positioning captures a parallel Hispanic demand pool a generic clinic would not

cons.claim: Community-expander demand is durable but not necessarily growing, so it can be mistaken for a growth lane
cons.example: treating the deep Assyrian base as license to add a seventh independent of any clinical format

failure_modes: assuming a large community implies unlimited format headroom rather than a stable parallel pool
crediting family loyalty as a moat while ignoring that succession can dissolve it
acceptance_tests: each community is given its cited share and the format(s) it anchors, and the bilingual/family-named practice evidence is named, distinguishing durable from growing demand
revisit_triggers: ancestry shares shift in a Census refresh
a community grows or contracts via migration
a multigenerational practice changes hands at succession

nodes.definition: Account for the single biggest cap on Turlock health demand: Modesto, ~15 minutes north, with Memorial/Doctors hospital systems, specialist optometry/ophthalmology, large multi-provider and DSO dental groups, and chain optical, pulls the higher-acuity and price-shopping demand out of Turlock. This leakage is the main reason the catalog's per-10k ratios sit below the U.S. provider benchmark even in a fully-served market, and it bites hardest on cross-shopped, higher-acuity clinical demand (complex dental, specialist eye care, hospital PT) while sparing neighborhood-loyal and community-anchored formats. Any format judgment that ignores this leakage will over-state Turlock headroom.

included: Modesto's size and proximity
which clinical demand leaks to it
which formats are most versus least exposed
excluded: the measured leakage magnitude (it is a behavioral estimate, not a count)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: regional clinical supply in Modesto or Turlock shifts

pros.claim: Naming the leakage explains why population alone over-predicts Turlock's provider count and why the catalog ratio sits below benchmark
pros.example: hospital and specialist PT demand leaks to Modesto, leaving Turlock PT under-built at 0.41/10k

cons.claim: The leakage is a behavioral estimate of cross-shopping, not a measured figure, so it can be over- or under-applied
cons.example: assuming all complex demand leaks when a since-1950 practice like Turlock Eyecare retains a loyal medical-eye-care base

failure_modes: applying the leakage cap uniformly to community-anchored formats that do not cross-shop
treating the leakage as measured when it is a behavioral estimate
acceptance_tests: the analysis states Modesto's size and distance and ranks formats by leakage exposure, flagging the magnitude as a behavioral estimate
revisit_triggers: a major clinical development opens in Modesto or Turlock
a cross-shop leakage study is produced
a hospital-system service line changes in either city

nodes.definition: Lay down the published, cited cost-structure backbone every format model is read against, split by engine. Clinical: dental overhead ~55-65% of collections (sub-$750k solo practices 70-80%; payroll 25-28%, lab 6-8%, supplies 5-6%, rent 6-7%); optometry optical COGS 27-35% of revenue; PT payroll ~70% of fixed overhead / 40-50% of total expenses, rent ~5-10%, supply COGS ~15%, revenue ~$75-$150/visit; chiropractic near-zero consumable COGS dominated by owner labor + rent + liability + EHR. Cash/wellness: gym and yoga near-zero COGS, payroll the largest line, lease #2, rent ~20-30% of revenue for yoga, instructor pay ~$25-$75/class. These are planning benchmarks, not audited operator P&Ls, and they are the lens that turns a revenue band into a margin reality.

included: overhead/COGS/payroll/net benchmark ranges by sub-category and engine
the dental overhead and optical COGS backbones
the planning-prior status of the figures

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a published cost-structure benchmark is revised

pros.claim: Pairing every revenue band with the overhead and net benchmark stops high gross from being mistaken for high profit
pros.example: a multi-provider dental office benchmarking $1M+ gross still runs 55-65% overhead, which the backbone makes explicit

cons.claim: Published benchmarks lag and average away the owner-labor and Valley-haircut effects that move real Turlock margins
cons.example: the 55-65% dental overhead benchmark understates cost for a sub-$750k Denti-Cal-heavy solo practice running 70-80%

failure_modes: importing a national benchmark without the Central-Valley reimbursement/cost-of-living haircut
reading a benchmark range as a single point estimate
acceptance_tests: overhead, COGS, payroll and net benchmark ranges are stated by sub-category and engine with sources and labeled as planning priors
revisit_triggers: a new ADA HPI or optometry/PT benchmark survey is published
a reimbursement or wage change shifts the payroll or overhead share
a profitability base-rate update lands

nodes.definition: Define the only honest way to attach a revenue band to a sub-category when no per-business revenue is public: take a published benchmark (dental $600k-$1.0M gross/single-dentist office; optometry $500k-$900k/single-OD; PT $150k-$300k/PT or ~$300k-$700k/clinic; chiropractic $150k-$450k gross/solo DC; gym/fitness $120k-$500k/studio; yoga $100k-$350k/studio) and scale it by an observable size signal (inferable provider count, format, single-versus-multi-provider, advertised procedure scope), apply a ~0.80-0.90 Central-Valley reimbursement/cost-of-living haircut, then tag the result 'estimate, not actual', assign a confidence level, and name the confirmation path (operator interviews, vendor invoices, county provider-enrollment and CDTFA/Turlock Finance receipts). High-gross multi-provider offices are paired with their thin-net overhead caveat so revenue is never read as profit.

included: benchmark-times-size-signal-times-Valley-haircut method
the estimate-not-actual label, confidence and confirmation path
the high-gross-versus-thin-net pairing
excluded: stating a named business's actual revenue or collections

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a benchmark, a size signal, or the availability of confirming receipts changes

pros.claim: A labeled benchmark band gives a defensible planning number without ever claiming a private practice's actual revenue
pros.example: a single-OD optometry practice scaled at $500k-$900k with the Valley haircut, tagged estimate with a confirmation path

cons.claim: A benchmark band can be over-trusted if the size signal is mis-observed or the confidence label is dropped
cons.example: treating an inferred single-dentist office as a fact when an associate doctor scales it toward the top of the band

failure_modes: dropping the estimate-not-actual label and presenting a band as a fact
applying a national benchmark without the Central-Valley haircut
acceptance_tests: every revenue band produced carries the estimate-not-actual label, a confidence level, the size signal used, the Valley haircut and a named confirmation source, and high gross is paired with the thin-net caveat
revisit_triggers: a published per-provider/per-practice/per-studio benchmark is updated
county provider-enrollment or CDTFA receipts become available
a sub-category's observable size signal changes

nodes.definition: Explain the binding constraint on the clinical engine: reimbursement, not input supply, is what compresses margin. Stanislaus is a high-Medi-Cal county that lost ~17,000 enrollees in the 2024 unwinding; Denti-Cal reimburses well below commercial PPO and carries heavier admin, capping how many dental and clinical independents can subsist on the low-income majority and pushing them toward PPO/cash share. The 2026 Medicare PT conversion factor (~$33.40, net ~-1% after RVU changes) is a per-visit headwind that means PT growth must come from referral volume, not rate. The formats most exposed are Denti-Cal-heavy dental, Medicare-exposed PT, and the insurance-billing slice of optometry; cash/maintenance chiropractic and the wellness engine are largely insulated.

included: the payer-mix cap and Denti-Cal-below-PPO compression
the 2026 Medicare conversion factor headwind
which clinical formats are most exposed
excluded: the input-supply cost (that is the supplier node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a Denti-Cal rate, Medi-Cal enrollment, or Medicare conversion factor changes

pros.claim: Naming reimbursement as the binding clinical constraint corrects the assumption that input cost sets clinical margin
pros.example: a Denti-Cal-heavy dental office is margin-capped by the rate, not by the price of composites or crowns

cons.claim: Reimbursement figures are dated facts in a moving system, so the constraint magnitude is current-snapshot not forward-fixed
cons.example: the 2026 conversion factor and the 2024 unwinding are as-of figures a future cycle will move

failure_modes: modeling a clinical format on input cost and missing that the payer rate is the binding cap
treating the 2026 cut as a permanent rather than a current-cycle figure
acceptance_tests: the analysis states the payer-mix cap, the Denti-Cal-below-PPO compression, the ~$33.40 2026 conversion factor and the most-exposed formats, flagging the figures as current-snapshot
revisit_triggers: a Denti-Cal rate or Medi-Cal enrollment change
a new Medicare conversion factor is set
a commercial PPO contract shift

nodes.definition: Quantify the supplier-concentration margin risk the demand view alone misses, concentrated in the capital-and-COGS-heavy clinical formats. Dental is dominated by the 'big three' (Henry Schein ~41%, Patterson ~34%, Benco ~10%, together ~85% of distributor sales); optical is dominated by EssilorLuxottica (frames + lenses) and ABB Optical (contacts, ~two-thirds of ECPs). These national distributors hold strong pricing power over small Turlock independents. The main counterweight is buying-group membership — Vision Source, PECAA, IDOC, EPON for optical; GPOs for dental — which pulls COGS toward the low end. Cash/membership formats avoid this entirely: their supply chain is durable capex bought once, with near-zero perishable inventory.

buying-group membership as the counterweight
why cash formats avoid the concentration
excluded: the named supplier-to-business links (that is the supply-chain map)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a distributor share, buying group, or contract price materially changes

pros.claim: Surfacing distributor concentration shows a real margin risk the per-capita demand read entirely misses
pros.example: the dental big-three's ~85% share gives them pricing power over a solo Turlock practice absent GPO membership

cons.claim: Concentration shares are national and the buying-group offset is variable, so the squeeze magnitude is directional not exact
cons.example: an IDOC or Vision Source member pulling optical COGS to the low end versus a non-member paying list

failure_modes: ignoring distributor pricing power when modeling dental/optical margin
assuming buying-group membership fully neutralizes the squeeze
acceptance_tests: the dental big-three and EssilorLuxottica/ABB shares are stated, buying-group membership is named as the counterweight, and the cash-format exemption is distinguished
revisit_triggers: a distributor merger or share shift
a buying group enters or exits the Valley

nodes.definition: Establish the baseline licensing every clinical provider must clear through the California Department of Consumer Affairs healing-arts boards, plus the city of Turlock business license. Board of Chiropractic Examiners: annual DC renewal, 24 CE hours/yr (incl. 2 hrs Ethics & Law); X-ray practice adds RHB radiologic-equipment registration. Dental Board of California: DDS/RDH licensure, X-ray/CBCT registration, OSHA/Cal-OSHA infection control, biohazard waste handling. Board of Optometry: exam app fee $275, biennial renewal $500; glaucoma/TPA certifications expand billable medical scope. PT Board of California: app fee $300, initial license $150, $200 renewal, with limited direct access. These board gates plus professional liability (~$1,200/mo benchmark for solo clinical) are the real entry mechanics a pure demand analysis omits.

included: the four healing-arts boards and their fees/CE
X-ray/CBCT and RHB registration
professional liability and the city business license

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a healing-arts board fee, CE, or registration requirement changes

pros.claim: Treating the board gates as the mandatory clinical floor prevents a model that ignores CE, X-ray registration and liability
pros.example: a chiropractic X-ray practice budgeting RHB radiologic-equipment registration on top of DC renewal

cons.claim: The board fees are modest, so they can lull an entrant into underestimating the costlier Denti-Cal-enrollment and equipment gates
cons.example: assuming a $500 optometry renewal means easy entry while EssilorLuxottica COGS and equipment dominate

failure_modes: skipping X-ray/CBCT registration or CE compliance and risking board action
confusing the cheap board license with the costlier Denti-Cal-enrollment or capex gates
acceptance_tests: the four board gates, their fees/CE, X-ray/CBCT and RHB registration, liability and the city license are stated with their public sources as the mandatory clinical floor
revisit_triggers: a board fee or CE schedule changes
an X-ray/CBCT registration rule changes
a malpractice premium benchmark shifts

nodes.definition: Define the gate that separates dental licensure from the ability to bill the low-income majority: Denti-Cal/Medi-Cal dental provider enrollment is required to bill and is separate from DDS licensure. In a high-Medi-Cal county like Stanislaus this is the decisive payer-mix decision — Denti-Cal reimburses well below commercial PPO and carries heavier admin, so the choice of how much Denti-Cal volume to carry sets the dental practice's margin and overhead load. Practices escape Denti-Cal-rate commoditization by leaning into PPO/cash share and cosmetic/Invisalign/oral-surgery upsell (American Family Dentistry's family/cosmetic/Invisalign, Turlock Smiles' oral surgery). The enrollment-and-mix decision, not the supply chain, is the binding entry mechanic for an independent general-dental office.

included: Denti-Cal enrollment separate from licensure
the payer-mix margin decision
the PPO/cash and cosmetic-upsell escape from Denti-Cal rates
excluded: the dental equipment capex (in the dental model)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a Denti-Cal rate, enrollment rule, or county payer-mix changes

pros.claim: Identifying Denti-Cal enrollment as the binding dental gate corrects the assumption that licensure alone enables billing the local majority
pros.example: a Turlock dental office deciding its Denti-Cal-versus-PPO mix is setting its margin before any chair is bought

cons.claim: The right Denti-Cal mix is practice-specific, so this is a structural decision not a single recommended ratio
cons.example: a community-serving practice carrying heavy Denti-Cal versus a cosmetic-led one carrying almost none

failure_modes: budgeting licensure but not the Denti-Cal enrollment and its admin load
modeling dental margin on supply cost while the payer mix actually sets it
acceptance_tests: Denti-Cal enrollment is stated as separate from licensure, the payer-mix margin decision is named, and the PPO/cash and cosmetic-upsell escape is identified with its source
revisit_triggers: a Denti-Cal rate or enrollment-rule change
a Medi-Cal enrollment swing in the county
a practice shifts its payer mix

nodes.definition: Establish the binding non-fee gate for the cash/wellness engine: California AB-5 (Dynamex/ABC test) worker-classification exposure on the 1099 per-class-paid instructor model that gyms, barre and yoga studios run. Instructor pay scales with class volume and is frequently paid 1099, which is precisely where AB-5 misclassification risk bites — back-pay, payroll-tax and penalty exposure on reclassification. Studios also carry general liability (slip/fall, equipment) and ADA facility compliance, and the city of Turlock business license, but unlike clinical formats they face no healing-arts board. The W-2-versus-1099 instructor question is the structural gate every studio entrant (Barre Defined, Curl Fitness, Workout Studio by KB, I Am Yoga, the fitness arm of Elite PT & Fitness) must resolve before scaling.

general liability and ADA compliance for studios
the W-2-versus-1099 decision as the binding studio gate
excluded: the studio unit economics (in the studio models)

pros.claim: Identifying AB-5 as the binding studio gate corrects the 'low-capex means easy entry' illusion with a real classification risk
pros.example: a barre studio scaling its 1099 instructor roster faces reclassification back-pay exposure before it grows

cons.claim: AB-5 application is fact-specific, so the exposure is a structural risk whose magnitude depends on the instructor arrangement
cons.example: a studio with genuinely independent contractors versus one whose instructors meet employee tests

failure_modes: scaling a 1099 instructor roster without resolving the AB-5 classification question
treating low capex as easy entry while the classification gate is unaddressed
acceptance_tests: AB-5/Dynamex exposure on 1099 instructors, studio general liability and ADA compliance are stated with sources, and the W-2-versus-1099 question is identified as the binding studio gate
revisit_triggers: an AB-5 statute or case-law change

a misclassification enforcement action lands

nodes.definition: Map the capital-equipment intensity that gates format entry independent of demand, ranking the capex tiers high-to-low: dental ≈ optometry > PT > chiropractic ≈ gym > yoga. Dental needs chairs/units, digital pano/CBCT X-ray, autoclave and intraoral scanners — a high six-figure build-out; optometry needs a phoropter, auto-refractor, OCT/fundus camera, edger and exam lanes. PT needs treatment tables, an exercise floor and modalities (~$50k-$150k initial). Chiropractic needs adjusting tables ($1k-$5k each), modalities and optional digital X-ray ($40k-$80k for insurance/PI practices). Gym/fitness ranges $8k-$10k (small studio) to $100k+ (full floor), often leased to spread capex; yoga is the lowest capex in the sector (flooring, mirrors, sound, optional heat). Two formats can face the same demand but very different up-front capital, so capex is a real go/no-go input beside licensing.

nodes.definition: Model the independent dental practice (American Family Dentistry, Hawkeye Family Dental, Healthy Smile Dental, Melgosa Dental, Turlock Family Dentistry, Turlock Smiles Dentistry, Valley Dental Turlock). It is the most capital- and COGS-heavy clinical format: a high-six-figure build-out (chairs, CBCT, autoclave, scanners) and consumables plus lab fees as the cost center. It runs W-2 DDS/RDH and support staff with payroll the single largest cost line. It benchmarks $600k-$1.0M gross/single-dentist office, with multi-provider/oral-surgery offices (e.g., Turlock Smiles) scaling toward/above the top (estimate-not-actual, med confidence). Overhead is ~55-65% of collections (sub-$750k solo 70-80%), so high gross is not high net. Margin is set by the Denti-Cal-versus-PPO mix, not by supply; it is the most contested sub-category at 0.97/10k, winning on relationship/longevity and cosmetic upsell.

nodes.definition: Model the independent optometry practice (Avak's, Generations Family, Monte Vista, Plett Family, Turlock Eyecare since 1950, Turlock Family Vision). The exam is near-break-even; the margin engine is eyewear capture — frames, lenses and contacts at 27-35% optical COGS, pulled toward the low end by buying-group membership (Vision Source/PECAA/IDOC/EPON). It runs W-2 OD plus opticians and support, with a solo-OD income benchmark ~$212k, and benchmarks $500k-$900k revenue/single-OD practice (estimate-not-actual, med confidence). The defining threat is product-margin defense against Costco/online eyewear (Warby Parker, 1-800-Contacts) that bleeds the eyewear margin funding the practice; differentiation into medical eye care and specialty contact-lens fitting (Monte Vista, Avak's) is the survival move. At 0.83/10k it is crowded for independents and near its contested ceiling.

nodes.definition: Model the physical-therapy clinic (Altruistic PT, Elite PT & Fitness which straddles into the cash fitness engine, Tower PT). Payroll is ~70% of fixed overhead / 40-50% of total expenses; rent ~5-10%; admin (billing/marketing/software) ~10-15%; supply COGS ~15%. Two distinct anchors must not be quoted interchangeably: ~$75-$150/visit (billing 3-4 codes/session) and $150k-$300k revenue/PT or ~$300k-$700k/clinic (estimate-not-actual, med). The rule of thumb is a treating PT bills 3-4x salary and a clinic needs ~200-400 visits/month to break even. The 2026 Medicare cut (~$33.40 conversion factor, net ~-1%) is a per-visit headwind, so growth must come from physician-referral relationships and visit volume, not rate. At 0.41/10k it is the clearest under-built white space, with ortho/sports/post-surgical the opening.

nodes.definition: Model the chiropractic format (Atkinson, Beech, Crawford Chiropractic Center, LOR, Mas Vida, Turlock Auto Accident Injury / Dr. Greg Jones). It is segmented by model, and that segmentation is what keeps six clinics viable at 0.83/10k: wellness-cash (Atkinson, Beech), affordability-positioned (Crawford), bilingual (Mas Vida, English/Spanish), and auto-injury/lien (Dr. Jones). It runs predominantly owner-operator DC, often solo or +1 chiropractic assistant plus billing, with low consumable COGS; cost is dominated by owner labor + rent + professional liability + EHR ($300-$800/mo). It benchmarks $150k-$450k gross/solo DC, with auto-injury/lien clinics running higher and lumpier (settlement-timed) (estimate-not-actual, low-med). Cash/maintenance models carry minimal billing overhead; PI/auto trades higher per-case value for lien/collections risk and slower cash conversion.

nodes.definition: Model the independent gym/fitness studio (Barre Defined, Curl Fitness with Pilates and yoga, Workout Studio by KB with cardio/kettlebell/CrossFit/Pilates/personal training, plus the fitness arm of Elite PT & Fitness). It runs near-zero COGS: payroll is the largest line, lease #2, and lease + equipment ≈ 60-70% of startup cost, with equipment leasing converting capex to opex. The margin lever is utilization — members per square foot and class fill rate. It runs owner-operator plus per-class-paid instructors, frequently 1099 (AB-5 exposure), with instructor pay scaling to class volume. It benchmarks $120k-$500k revenue/studio with an owner take ~$50k-$120k (estimate-not-actual, low-med). At 0.41/10k it is thin because national chains own the value tier, so independents survive only as differentiated boutiques.

nodes.definition: Model the yoga/wellness studio (I Am Yoga Wellness Studio, offering Vinyasa, Ashtanga, Hatha, Restorative, Qi Gong, Yoga Sculpt and Pilates — straddling into the fitness-studio format). It is the lowest-capex format in the sector (flooring, mirrors, sound, optional heat) with near-zero perishable inventory. Rent runs ~20-30% of revenue; instructor pay ~$25-$75/class (≈30%+ of top-line, often 1099 with AB-5 exposure); the target is ~30-50% gross margin per class, with unlimited memberships ~$100-$200/mo. A broad format menu spreads fixed cost across more class slots. It benchmarks $100k-$350k revenue/studio (61% of US yoga studios earn <$500k/yr) (estimate-not-actual, med). At 0.14/10k it is the thinnest sub-category, with 1-2 more able to fit on the CSU + community base only if a new studio recaptures demand that gyms selling yoga/Pilates currently bleed off.

nodes.definition: Model the two dual-category businesses that sit in both economic engines at once and distort any strict per-sub-category tally. Elite Physical Therapy & Fitness straddles insurance-reimbursed PT and cash fitness, so it carries both a DME/modality clinical supply chain and a gym-equipment capex line, and both a payer-billing and a membership revenue stream. I Am Yoga Wellness Studio lists Pilates and Yoga Sculpt alongside Vinyasa/Ashtanga/Hatha/Restorative/Qi Gong/Qi-Gong, adding light equipment to an otherwise prop-only base and overlapping the fitness-studio format. The honest headline of '26 across six sub-categories' is bi-modal underneath for these two: each must be modeled as two cost-and-revenue arms, not one, and each is double-counted if a strict per-category sum is taken. Saturation reads are unaffected, but the unit-economics model for these two must split the clinical/cash arms.

nodes.definition: Encode the binding honesty protocol that travels with every number in this KB: per-business revenue, margin, payer mix, lease rate and staffing are NOT public for these privately held independents, so no dollar figure is ever stated as an actual reported figure for any named business. nodes.definition: Compose the merged go/no-go verdict on adding or running a given format, the synthesis the whole KB builds toward. It intersects three lenses: demand headroom (SATURATION_WHITESPACE), the cost/licensing gate (HEALING_ARTS_LICENSE, DENTICAL_ENROLLMENT, AB5_CLASSIFICATION, EQUIPMENT_CAPEX), and the margin reality (COST_STRUCTURE_BENCHMARKS, REIMBURSEMENT_CONSTRAINT), with every number carrying the HONESTY_LABEL. The reconciled rule: do not add a seventh chiropractic, a seventh independent optometry, or an eighth Denti-Cal-volume general-dental office; the defensible headroom is differentiated referral-driven PT, a second yoga/wellness studio that recaptures gym-bled demand, and niche bilingual or PI chiropractic — each viable only after clearing the board/Denti-Cal/AB-5 gate and the capex line. A white space that is demand-true but cost- or reimbursement-gated is a no-go until the gate is cleared.

conflict_axes.resolution_hint: apply community depth to neighborhood-loyal anchored formats and the Modesto cap to discretionary higher-acuity cross-shopped ones

conflict_axes.name: demand_headroom_vs_cost_reimbursement_gate
conflict_axes.description: A format with real demand headroom may still be gated by licensing, AB-5, capex or reimbursement, so demand-true is not the same as enterable.
poles: enter only where the gate clears
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat a demand-true but cost- or reimbursement-gated white space as a no-go until the binding gate is cleared

conflict_axes.name: high_gross_vs_thin_net
conflict_axes.description: High-revenue formats (multi-provider dental, full-eyewear optometry) can post strong gross while netting single digits, so revenue must never be read as profit.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always pair the revenue band with its overhead and net benchmark before judging attractiveness

conflict_axes.name: denti_cal_volume_vs_ppo_cash_margin
conflict_axes.description: Denti-Cal volume serves the low-income majority but reimburses below PPO with heavier admin, so volume and margin pull against each other.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: carry only the Denti-Cal share the overhead can absorb and use PPO/cash and cosmetic upsell for net

conflict_axes.name: reimbursement_rate_vs_referral_volume
conflict_axes.description: The 2026 Medicare cut compresses per-visit PT rate while the under-built PT white space rewards referral volume; rate and volume are the competing growth paths.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: grow PT on physician-referral relationships and visit volume, not on rate, given the conversion-factor headwind

conflict_axes.name: w2_clinical_vs_1099_studio_labor
conflict_axes.description: Clinical formats run W-2 licensed staff and carry payroll as the dominant cost, while studios run 1099 per-class instructors and carry AB-5 reclassification risk; the labor-model trade differs by engine.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: model clinical payroll as the dominant fixed cost and resolve the studio W-2-versus-1099 AB-5 question before scaling instructors

conflict_axes.name: buying_group_cost_lever_vs_distributor_power
conflict_axes.description: National distributor pricing power squeezes small-independent dental and optical COGS while buying-group membership pulls it back; the cost lever offsets but does not erase the power.
poles: join a buying group for cost
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat buying-group membership as the main counterweight to distributor power but not a full neutralizer of the squeeze

conflict_axes.name: cash_engine_utilization_vs_idle_fixed_cost
conflict_axes.description: The cash/wellness engine lives on utilization (members/sqft, class fill) while carrying lease and payroll as fixed cost regardless of fill, so a half-full studio drags net.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: model the gym/yoga studio on realistic class-fill and members/sqft, not on a full-capacity assumption the fixed cost cannot survive

edge_cases.description: A named business's actual revenue, collections or payer mix is requested or asserted as fact
edge_cases.trigger: a question demands the real sales or owner income of a specific Turlock practice
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse to state actual revenue; provide only a labeled benchmark estimate with method, public source, confidence and a confirmation path

edge_cases.description: A Denti-Cal rate cut or Medi-Cal enrollment swing compresses a dental practice's margin
edge_cases.trigger: a Denti-Cal reimbursement change or a Medi-Cal unwinding-style enrollment loss
edge_cases.mitigation: re-balance the Denti-Cal-versus-PPO/cash mix and re-estimate margin against the new rate

edge_cases.description: Costco or online eyewear bleeds the optical margin that funds an independent OD practice
edge_cases.trigger: a chain/online-eyewear price shift draws frames/contacts purchases out of the practice
edge_cases.mitigation: defend eyewear capture via medical eye care and specialty contact-lens fitting and pull COGS down through buying-group membership

edge_cases.description: A new Medicare conversion factor further cuts the PT per-visit rate
edge_cases.trigger: a Medicare physician/therapy fee-schedule update below the current ~$33.40
edge_cases.mitigation: grow on referral volume and visit count rather than rate, and re-check the ~200-400 visits/month break-even

edge_cases.description: A studio scales its 1099 instructor roster and triggers AB-5 reclassification exposure
edge_cases.trigger: a gym/barre/yoga studio grows its per-class 1099 instructor count past the ABC-test line
edge_cases.mitigation: resolve the W-2-versus-1099 classification before scaling and budget the reclassification/back-pay risk

edge_cases.description: A PI/auto-injury chiropractic clinic's lien collections slow and starve working capital
edge_cases.trigger: settlement timing lengthens on lien-based auto-injury cases
edge_cases.mitigation: model the PI/auto cash conversion separately from the cash/maintenance segment and carry working-capital reserve

edge_cases.description: A high multi-provider dental gross is read as high profit
edge_cases.trigger: a $1M+ dental gross band is quoted without the 55-65% overhead caveat
edge_cases.mitigation: pair every dental gross band with its overhead range and lead with the thin-net reality

edge_cases.description: The per-visit and per-PT-per-year benchmarks are quoted interchangeably
edge_cases.trigger: someone reads ~$120/visit as if it were the annual per-PT band
edge_cases.mitigation: keep the two anchors explicitly distinct and reconcile them only through visits-per-month, never substitute one for the other

edge_cases.description: A supplier-to-named-business link is upgraded from inference to a stated contract
edge_cases.trigger: an answer asserts a specific practice buys from a named distributor without a source
edge_cases.mitigation: keep supplier links labeled representative inference unless a cited source states the relationship

edge_cases.description: A demand-true white space is treated as enterable while a licensing, capex or reimbursement gate blocks it
edge_cases.trigger: a headroom call (PT, a second yoga studio) ignores the board/AB-5/capex/reimbursement gate
edge_cases.mitigation: run every white space through the cost/licensing/reimbursement gate before issuing a go verdict

edge_cases.description: A deep heritage community is treated as a growth lane when it only sustains a stable count
edge_cases.trigger: a large ancestry share is read as unlimited format headroom
edge_cases.mitigation: distinguish culturally durable demand from growing demand before recommending an addition

workflow.action: Size the resident, student, ag and retiree demand floor
workflow.description: State the population, income, student and musculoskeletal-demand figures and the clinical-versus-cash engine split as cited facts or labeled estimates
workflow.gate: population, income, enrollment, the ag/retiree musculoskeletal driver and the two-engine split are stated

workflow.description: Tie each ancestry share and family-dynasty loyalty to the formats it sustains
workflow.gate: each community has a cited share and named anchored formats with the bilingual/family evidence

workflow.description: Identify which clinical demand leaks to Modesto and which formats are exposed
workflow.gate: Modesto size/distance stated and formats ranked by leakage exposure as a behavioral estimate

workflow.description: State overhead/COGS/payroll/net benchmarks by sub-category and engine with sources
workflow.gate: overhead, COGS, payroll and net ranges are stated as cited planning priors

workflow.action: Set the labeled-estimate revenue method and honesty label
workflow.description: Define benchmark-times-size-signal-times-haircut banding with the estimate label, confidence and confirmation path
workflow.gate: every band carries the estimate-not-actual label, a confidence, a size signal, the Valley haircut and a confirmation source

workflow.action: Identify the reimbursement and supplier constraints
workflow.description: Explain the payer-mix cap, the 2026 Medicare cut and the distributor concentration with its buying-group offset
workflow.gate: the reimbursement cap, the conversion factor and the distributor concentration are stated

workflow.description: Name the dental, optical, chiro/PT-equipment and studio supplier and software nodes per format as inference
workflow.gate: each major format has named supplier nodes with the inference label

workflow.action: Establish the licensing, Denti-Cal, AB-5 and capex gates
workflow.description: State the board floor, the Denti-Cal enrollment gate, the AB-5 studio gate and the per-format capex
workflow.gate: the board gates, Denti-Cal enrollment, AB-5 exposure and capex intensity are stated with sources

workflow.description: For each sub-category, state offering, cost center, labor model, benchmark band and the gate or constraint that decides viability
workflow.gate: each format names its cost center, labeled band and the gate or constraint that decides viability

workflow.action: Synthesize the per-sub-category saturation and white space
workflow.description: Give the per-10k at-ceiling/under-built read and rank the white space with the provider-versus-business caveat
workflow.gate: each sub-category has a saturation read and the white space is ranked

workflow.action: Issue the merged format go/no-go verdict
workflow.description: Intersect demand headroom, cost/licensing/reimbursement gate and margin reality into an add/avoid call carrying the honesty label
workflow.gate: the verdict states the saturation read, binding gate and margin reality, is conditioned on clearing the board/Denti-Cal/AB-5 gate, and every number carries the estimate-not-actual label

priority_rationale: The demand floor, community anchors and Modesto leakage come first because every format judgment depends on knowing the size and shape of demand and the two economic engines; the cost-structure backbone, labeled-revenue method, reimbursement and supplier constraints and supplier map next, because they are the lenses that turn demand into unit economics and the honesty label that keeps every number defensible; the board, Denti-Cal, AB-5 and capex gates next, because they decide enterability independent of demand; the six sub-category format models then apply all of that to the named businesses; and the saturation synthesis and merged go/no-go come last because they compose every upstream output into a defensible add/avoid verdict.

dominance_rules.rule: The honesty label dominates any revenue claim
dominance_rules.rationale: no per-business revenue, margin or payer mix is public, so a band may never be presented as an actual figure for a named business
dominance_rules.trigger: any dollar figure is attached to a named business or sub-category
dominance_rules.action: tag it estimate-not-actual with a method, public source, confidence and confirmation path, and refuse an actual-revenue claim

dominance_rules.rule: The cost/licensing/reimbursement gate dominates demand headroom in any entry verdict
dominance_rules.rationale: a demand-true white space that cannot clear board licensing, Denti-Cal enrollment, AB-5 or capex is not enterable
dominance_rules.trigger: a go recommendation rests on demand alone
dominance_rules.action: withhold the go until the binding gate is shown clearable

dominance_rules.rule: Net margin dominates gross revenue in judging attractiveness
dominance_rules.rationale: high-gross clinical formats still net only single digits after 55-65% overhead, so revenue must not be read as profit
dominance_rules.trigger: a format is judged by its revenue band alone
dominance_rules.action: pair the band with its overhead and net benchmark before deciding

dominance_rules.rule: Reimbursement dominates input supply as the clinical margin constraint
dominance_rules.rationale: Denti-Cal rates and the 2026 Medicare cut move clinical margin more than any consumable cost
dominance_rules.trigger: a clinical format is modeled on input cost
dominance_rules.action: model the payer mix and reimbursement rate as the binding margin constraint

dominance_rules.rule: The Denti-Cal mix decision dominates the dental margin
dominance_rules.rationale: the below-PPO Denti-Cal rate and admin load set the dental practice's overhead and net
dominance_rules.trigger: a dental model omits the payer-mix decision
dominance_rules.action: set the Denti-Cal-versus-PPO/cash mix before estimating margin

dominance_rules.rule: The AB-5 classification gate dominates the low-capex studio illusion
dominance_rules.rationale: low capex makes a studio look easy to enter while the 1099 classification risk is the real scaling gate
dominance_rules.trigger: a studio is judged on capex alone
dominance_rules.action: resolve the W-2-versus-1099 AB-5 question before treating the studio as easy to scale

dominance_rules.rule: Saturation dominates demand depth for at-ceiling sub-categories
dominance_rules.rationale: a deep community base does not justify adding to a contested near-ceiling count
dominance_rules.trigger: an addition is proposed for optometry, independent dental or undifferentiated chiropractic
dominance_rules.action: default to no-add and defend the existing count on differentiation

dominance_rules.rule: Eyewear capture dominates the exam in judging optometry margin
dominance_rules.rationale: the exam is near-break-even and the 27-35% optical COGS is recovered only on captured eyewear
dominance_rules.trigger: optometry margin is read from the exam fee
dominance_rules.action: model the eyewear-capture rate and optical COGS as the margin engine

dominance_rules.rule: Documented links dominate inferred supplier links
dominance_rules.rationale: supplier-to-named-business links are representative inference unless a cited source states the relationship
dominance_rules.action: label it inference unless a cited source documents it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attach the estimate-not-actual label when the band is first produced, not after review
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a revenue figure circulating as a fact for a named practice and having to be retracted

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the Denti-Cal-versus-PPO mix before estimating a dental practice's margin
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a dental model built on supply cost that must be redone once the payer mix is seen to set margin

anti_rework_rules.rule: Resolve the W-2-versus-1099 AB-5 question before scoping a studio scale-up
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a studio scaling its 1099 roster and then facing reclassification back-pay it never budgeted

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pair every revenue band with its overhead and net benchmark in the same step
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a high-gross clinical format being approved before the thin net is seen

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep the per-visit and per-PT-per-year PT anchors distinct from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: the two reconcilable-but-distinct benchmarks being quoted interchangeably and the PT model being re-derived

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run a white space through the licensing/AB-5/capex/reimbursement gate before calling it an opportunity
anti_rework_rules.prevents: recommending a demand-true but gated format and reversing the call

anti_rework_rules.rule: Apply the Central-Valley reimbursement/cost-of-living haircut when the band is first scaled
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a national-benchmark band being used unadjusted and re-haircut later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep supplier-to-business links labeled inference from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an inferred supply link hardening into an asserted contract that must later be corrected

anti_rework_rules.rule: Report coverage as a floor of at least 26, not a census, from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an exact-universe claim that a later-found independent forces to be retracted

iteration_protocol.trigger: primary outreach, vendor invoices, or county provider-enrollment / CDTFA / Turlock Finance receipts become available
iteration_protocol.action: replace the labeled revenue bands and payer-mix estimates with confirmed figures and re-rank confidence

iteration_protocol.trigger: a Census ACS refresh changes population, income or ancestry shares
iteration_protocol.action: re-size the demand floor and re-map the community anchors and saturation reads

iteration_protocol.trigger: a Denti-Cal rate, Medi-Cal enrollment, or Medicare PT conversion-factor change lands
iteration_protocol.action: update the reimbursement constraint and the dental and PT format margins

iteration_protocol.trigger: a distributor merger or buying-group change shifts dental/optical COGS
iteration_protocol.action: update the supplier-concentration and supply-chain nodes and the dental and optometry models

iteration_protocol.trigger: an AB-5 statute or case-law change, or a board fee/CE change
iteration_protocol.action: re-evaluate the studio classification and clinical licensing gates and the affected format verdicts

iteration_protocol.trigger: a practice or studio opens or closes, changing a per-sub-category count
iteration_protocol.action: update the saturation read and the merged go/no-go for that sub-category

iteration_protocol.trigger: a cross-shop leakage study or measured Modesto-capture figure is produced
iteration_protocol.action: replace the behavioral leakage estimate and re-rank the at-ceiling sub-categories

iteration_protocol.trigger: an equipment-cost or financing/leasing change moves a format's capex
iteration_protocol.action: update the capex intensity and any format whose entry the change affects
